claims.text: The material is a solid-solution high-entropy alloy containing at least five elements at concentrations of at least 5 atomic percent each.
Superconducting behavior in the alloy is governed by formation of a specific short-range-order structure.
High pressure stabilizes the proposed short-range-order structure.
Low temperature stabilizes the proposed short-range-order structure.
Stabilization of the short-range-order structure enhances superconducting behavior.
At 10 GPa and 4 K, the superconducting critical temperature will increase by 20% relative to the baseline.
The proposed pressure and temperature boundary conditions are 0–20 GPa and 4–300 K.
The alloy's exact composition may affect formation and stability of the short-range-order structure.
The alloy's processing history may affect formation and stability of the short-range-order structure.
Differences in short-range-order formation and stability caused by composition or processing history may alter superconducting behavior.
Failure of Tc at 10 GPa and 4 K to exceed Tc at 0 GPa and 4 K by at least 15% would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The baseline is defined as Tc at ambient pressure and ambient temperature, whereas the controlled comparison uses 0 GPa and 4 K. These are not the same baseline conditions.

The stated prediction is a 20% Tc increase, but the falsification rule accepts any increase of at least 15%; therefore an observation between 15% and 20% misses the quantitative prediction without falsifying the hypothesis.
